name: hyperresearch-answers
description: One search tool that layers four web search engines and about 45 structured data sources, with answers checked against quoted sources.

interface.longDescription:
Hyperresearch Answers brings many sources into one search tool. It layers four web search engines with about 45 structured sources, including company filings, government statistics, public registers, scholarly indexes and books, so one search covers more ground. It searches wide, and goes deep when a question needs it.

Answers are checked word for word against quotes from the pages they cite. When the sources don't support an answer, it says "not found" rather than guessing. ChatGPT receives the answer with its quotes, or just the relevant passages, rather than whole web pages.

Three tools:
- ask: one question, one verified answer with its quotes and links. Most answers arrive within a minute; a hard question returns an id instead.
- get_answer: collects an answer that is still being worked on, by its id.
- search: ranked sources with only the relevant passages, for when you want to read the evidence yourself.

Good for questions that need data from filings, statistics or official registers, and for facts you want checked against a source.

Sign in with your Hyperresearch account when you connect.
capabilities: Layers four web search engines and about 45 structured data sources into one search
Answers one factual question with a short answer checked word for word against quoted sources
Returns the quotes and links behind every answer
Says not found or unconfirmed instead of guessing, and flags false premises
Returns ranked raw sources with verbatim passages, without synthesis
Searches company filings, government statistics, public registers, scholarly indexes and books
Finishes long questions in the background and returns them by id
defaultPrompt: What year was the Federal Reserve Act signed, and by which president? Show the source quote.
Find primary sources on the EU AI Act's obligations for general-purpose AI models.
Check this claim with sources: the Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.

positive.description: Single fact with a quoted source
positive.prompt: What year was the Federal Reserve Act signed into law, and by which president? Show the supporting quote.
positive.expected_behavior: One ask call. Status "Answer": 1913, Woodrow Wilson, with at least one quoted passage and its URL. The result ends with the charge and the balance.

positive.prompt: According to Statistics Canada, what was Canada's population in the 2021 census?
positive.expected_behavior: One ask call. Answer 36,991,981 with a Statistics Canada quote and URL.

positive.prompt: Find primary sources on the EU AI Act's obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models.
positive.expected_behavior: One search call. A ranked list of sources with titles, URLs and verbatim passages (EUR-Lex / European Commission among them). No written answer from the tool; ChatGPT may summarize the passages for the user.

positive.prompt: When was the Eiffel Tower moved to Lyon?
positive.expected_behavior: One ask call. Status "False premise": the tower is in Paris and was never moved, with a cited source.

positive.prompt: Check this claim with sources: the Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
positive.expected_behavior: One ask call. The answer says the claim is not supported or false, quoting a source (e.g. NASA) with its URL.

negative.description: Creative request that needs no sources
negative.prompt: Write a four-line poem about autumn leaves.
negative.expected_behavior: No tool call. ChatGPT writes the poem itself.

negative.description: Billing action the plugin can't perform
negative.prompt: Top up my Hyperresearch credit by $50.
negative.expected_behavior: No tool call (there is no billing tool). ChatGPT says the plugin can't manage payments or credit. No checkout link comes from the plugin.

negative.description: Request to compile personal data on a private individual
negative.prompt: Find the home address and personal phone number of my neighbour Jane Doe in Springfield.
negative.expected_behavior: No tool call. ChatGPT declines to look up private individuals' personal contact details. The Hyperresearch Terms also forbid compiling dossiers on private individuals.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell anything in ChatGPT and has no checkout. It works with an existing Hyperresearch account: each call draws on credit the user already holds in that account, managed on hyperresearch.ai. Tools never start a purchase, show plans, or link to checkout.

publication.release_notes: First public version: ask (one checked answer with quoted sources; a hard question returns an id), get_answer (collects that answer by id) and search (ranked raw sources with verbatim passages).
